behaviors.current: Routes require a bearer token. The OpenAI-Beta header is accepted and ignored on every route (decision 2026-10-12): the pinned SDK sends it on Agents API calls, and other clients need not, so every operation answers the same with or without it (swept both ways). Every implemented operation answers a missing token with 401, placeholder IDs with 404, and invalid bodies with 400, all in the public error shape (raw HTTP sweep driven by this inventory). Project API keys carry permissions (api.agents.*, api.responses.write, api.vaults.*, api.files.*, and the local api.webhooks.*): a missing permission answers 403 naming it, and another project's resource answers 404, swept over every implemented operation.
behaviors.remaining: None within the parity target. The guides publish no per-operation error matrix (see contract_shape.error_source), so error bodies are checked for the public shape.

behaviors.current: Saved and inline fields preserve omitted values, replace supplied objects, and reset nulls. Provider requests verify effort, summary, text, and auto/default/flex/priority tiers across cold resume.
behaviors.remaining: Session updates change only model, effort, and tier for later turns; provider-specific model compatibility remains. Prototype limits no longer apply to the public routes.

behaviors.current: Agents, sessions, and vaults (every resource that takes metadata) share one validator: at most 16 string pairs, keys up to 64 and values up to 512 characters (counted as characters, not bytes). Omitted preserves, null/empty clears, supplied objects replace. The SDK covers unicode limits and invalid updates; a boundary test checks the limits and one past them on all five create and update operations.
behaviors.remaining: None. Metadata is validated identically on every resource that takes it, and resources are project-scoped (G13).

behaviors.current: Every list orders by a monotonic creation sequence (skill versions by version number), so ordering is stable, cursors are exclusive, and an ascending walk is the reverse of a descending one; lists default to desc where the SDK offers order. A walk test pages agents, sessions, vaults, credentials, files, skills, skill versions, and webhook endpoints one item at a time and checks first_id, last_id, and has_more; items, turns, and subagents are walked where they are produced. Each list applies its documented limits: vault, credential, and webhook endpoint lists clamp limit to 1..100, file lists allow 1..10000, environment files use opaque page tokens, and the rest reject limits outside 1..100. Unknown or deleted cursors are rejected, sessions filter by agent_id, and every list and cursor is scoped to the caller's project.

Batches of 1-32 events are validated whole, then run in order: tool results plus at most one message or cancel. Messages carry text and data-URL images. Idempotency-Key is scoped to the session, retained 24 hours, replays stored outcomes, rejects different reuse (400) and concurrent use (409), and reports interrupted dispatch as unknown (409) without re-running. Input that steers a turn as it ends gets a follow-up turn rather than being recorded unanswered; a cancel sent before Codex reports a just-started turn still stops it. Initial input on a self_hosted session waits behind an environment_connection action like later input.
behaviors.remaining: None within the parity target. The public docs define neither batch nor idempotency semantics, so these are the contract by decision (2026-10-12).

behaviors.current: Streams are live-only and close on lag (1,024-event buffer), backend loss, or session deletion. Items follow the SDK added/part/delta/done order; terminal turns close unfinished items as incomplete; a documented subscribe/read/merge recovery reproduces saved items. Eight concurrent sessions keep their inputs apart while a subscriber never reads.
behaviors.remaining: None. Streams are live-only by contract and never promise replay.

behaviors.current: All pinned SDK tool configuration variants persist and round trip. Public HTTP MCP servers execute as session-scoped Codex servers with allowed_tools, non-secret HTTP headers that round trip, write-only encrypted authorization, vault credentials, required-server failed turns, and egress checks. Inline transport.authorization is encrypted with stdio secrets and snapshotted per session: bare tokens use Bearer, explicit schemes survive, empty values and credential_id conflicts return 400, and inline values win over auto-matched credentials. An Authorization header is refused; use transport.authorization. request_metadata maps to codex-config request_meta and tools/call _meta with Codex keys winning collisions. Authorization and metadata survive agent deletion and cold resume (mock MCP evidence, 2026-10-12). Self-hosted stdio and environment-origin HTTP servers execute on the caller's executor, outside service egress policy. Built-in web search maps every setting onto Codex and records web_search_call items; provider support remains required and cached is refused on self_hosted. Programmatic calling maps to sandboxed V8 code mode with nested function calls, fail-closed host execution, cancellation, and model tool_mode precedence/refusals (mock provider and real host, 2026-10-12). Compaction is automatic with no public controls/items; cold resume retains compacted model context and full public history. Skills/plugins isolation verified locally 2026-10-13: two sessions receive only their own capability-directory skills, plugin skills, and pinned Skills API versions before and after API/worker restart and executor reconnection; later defaults do not replace the pins (mock provider).

multi_agent enables Codex's V2 multi-agent runtime with max_concurrent_subagents + 1 threads (the root counts). Subagents are registered from spawn activity, emit subagent.created, have no function tools, and their turns and items are recorded apart from root history and stream tagged with subagent_id. Their usage counts toward the session. Deletion refuses while a subagent is active. Cancellation interrupts running subagent turns, and restarted sessions resume existing subagents under the same IDs.
behaviors.remaining: None within the parity target. create_subagent_call carries the model and reasoning effort Codex resolves at spawn, and tasks, messages, and results between agents are agent_message items. Subagent task text in call items, wait_for_subagents/close/resume items, and closed status are not reported by Codex V2; accepted as engine limits (decision 2026-10-12).

behaviors.current: Self-hosted sessions record an environment, report pending/connected/disconnected/failed events, and attach it to the worker through the service's registry and Noise rendezvous relay. Input while the executor is offline waits up to five minutes behind an environment_connection action, then starts in order; timed-out input is dropped and fails the session, never replayed. A command interrupted by executor loss is reported failed to the model after Codex's 25-second resume window and never re-run; a new executor and a replaced worker continue the session in the same workspace; a service restart fails input that was waiting. Cancel drops waiting input; deletion forgets the environment without stopping the caller's compute. capability_directories select skills and plugins on the executor, with the worker's own plugins kept off. The connection wait is an operator setting defaulting to five minutes. Executors authenticate with the operator's environment key or a project key holding api.environments.connect, which reaches only its project's environments. Skills/plugins isolation verified locally 2026-10-13: two sessions receive only their own capability-directory skills, plugin skills, and pinned Skills API versions before and after API/worker restart and executor reconnection; later defaults do not replace the pins (mock provider).

behaviors.current: Vault and credential metadata live in SQLite. Secret values are encrypted (age with scrypt) under an operator-supplied passphrase in the data directory, and are never returned, stored in public records, or sent to the model. Without a passphrase, credential operations return 501. Sessions attach vault_ids; each service-origin HTTP MCP server takes the credential its credential_id names or the only credential for its URL, and several matches are rejected. Each session snapshots its secrets at creation, so rotation and deletion affect only newer sessions. static_bearer tokens and mcp_oauth access tokens become the server's Authorization header.
behaviors.remaining: None within the parity target. environment_variable credentials and their networking restrictions need OpenAI-hosted environments (out of scope, 2026-10-06). OAuth token refresh and external key management are out of scope by decision (2026-10-12): callers rotate tokens through the credentials API. Inline MCP authorization is tracked with BEH-008.

behaviors.current: Webhook endpoints are managed through the SDK's /webhook_endpoints API, accepting the five agent.session.* event types and the 18 other event types the pinned SDK accepts (never produced here). Signing secrets are encrypted in the vault store and returned only at creation and rotation. Test deliveries are signed with the Standard Webhooks scheme the SDK verifies, go only to https public addresses (or operator-allowed hosts), connect to the checked addresses, and do not follow redirects. agent.session.created carries environment_id and environment_type, and connect.remote_url for a self-hosted environment; agent.session.action_required carries the session's first required action, a function_call or an environment_connection. Session status changes queue deliveries in the same transaction (outbox), delivered at least once with a stable webhook-id, retried with exponential backoff for 72 hours across restarts.
behaviors.remaining: None within the parity target. The guide promises no delivery order, so none is guaranteed after a failed attempt.
